newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq accuses Iran of meddling in its Kurdish affairs.
newsitem.headline: Iraq accuses Iran of meddling in its Kurdish affairs.

text.p: Iraq accused its neighbour Iran on Wednesday of interfering in its northern Kurdish areas and urged Tehran to steer away from fighting between rival factions there.

"This is not the first time Iran meddles in Iraq's domestic affairs in such a flagrant manner," Culture and Information Minister Hamed Youssef Hummadi said in a statement carried by the official Iraqi News Agency (INA).

Massoud Barzani, leader of the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP), has accused Iranian forces of entering northern Iraq to help rival guerrillas of the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) led by Jalal Talabani retake a key city on Sunday.
Both Iran and PUK have denied the charges but Hummadi said: "Iran's denial of involvement in the backing of Jalal Talabani's group in its armed struggle with Massoud Barzani cannot be substantiated."

Iraqi troops and tanks helped Barzani take control of much of northern Iraq in a lightning offensive against the PUK last month. The United States retaliated against Baghdad's move by launching missiles at military targets in southern Iraq and has since tried to mediate between the two Kurdish factions.

Barzani has called for outside help against Iran. Baghdad has called on both factions to solve their differences via dialogue and resume talks on some form of Kurdish autonomy with the central government.
The PUK has turned down the latest Iraqi overture. Iran has also called for peace talks between the two factions which have a long history of enmity and shifting alliances.

INA said Hummadi's remarks were in reaction to an interview by Iran's President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani published in the German magazine Der Spiegel and carried by the Iranian official news agency IRNA.
Hummadi uged Iran to review its policy towards Iraq and stay out of the "American ploy" in the north.
He asked Iran "to seriously work for a solution of the outstanding issues...for the ultimate establishment of natural relations between the two countries."
Iraq and Iran fought a ruinous war from 1980 to 1988 and despite a U.N.-brokered ceasefire the two countries are still at loggerheads over a host of issues.
